summary: The article argues that school boards and educational leaders must invest in strong cybersecurity for remote learning, given rising and increasingly sophisticated attacks on educational institutions. It outlines the costs of complacency and proposes a multi-faceted response: advanced technical defenses, comprehensive policies, awareness training, and engagement with external experts. It closes with a call to reassess budgets and prioritize cybersecurity.
one_line: An article urging school boards to invest in advanced defenses, policies, training and expert partnerships to protect remote learning from escalating cyber attacks.
key_facts: Dr. Elaine Suarez spoke at the EdTech Security Summit on September 15, 2023, about threats including phishing scams, ransomware, unauthorized access and data theft.
The Midlands Education Network breach, dated October 2023 in the article, compromised personal information of over 200,000 students and educators.
Cybersecurity law specialist Gregory Chen said schools not complying with data protection regulations face severe legal implications and fines that can cripple budgets.
The cost of ignoring cyber threats includes financial losses from downtime and ransom payments, legal ramifications, and damage to reputation and the trust of students and parents.

Michaela Francoise, CTO of SecureEdTech, highlights next-generation firewalls (NGFWs), intrusion prevention systems (IPS), and endpoint detection and response (EDR) tools as critical advanced solutions.
Cloud-based security platforms can provide scalable protection suited to the decentralized nature of remote learning and can detect patterns indicative of a cyber threat.
Policy advisor Jennifer Clarke said at the National Cybersecurity Education Conference on November 5, 2023, that clear policies set expectations and define what to do when they are not met.
Cybersecurity policies should define acceptable use, incident response procedures, and regular audits, and should include vendor management for third-party providers handling student and staff data.
As of December 2023, over 90% of cyber incidents in education were attributed to user mistakes, according to a report by the Alliance for Safer Schools Online (ASSO).
The State School District of Jefferson County uses cyber drills and gamified learning experiences that have shown to enhance cybersecurity practices significantly.
External cybersecurity experts can offer tailored strategies, vulnerability assessments, and continuous monitoring and updating of security protocols.
The article calls on school boards to reassess budgets, redirect resources, and prioritize cybersecurity.
